title: TDDR Rising Narratives — Thanksgiving evening, Nov 26
summary: A snapshot of opposition narratives from the Right and the Far Left as of 5:25 PM ET Thursday, Nov 26, 2026 (Thanksgiving). Built for TDDR (Too Dumb Didn't Read). The 'USAID Files' censorship story is now the largest query (25,038 posts in 24 hours, 7.84×) and held near Wednesday's pace on the holiday; the files' most-cited item is still a 2022 proposal that, per reviews of the release, was never funded. New on the Right: Trump's Thanksgiving post thanking 'those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election' after a routine GDP revision (7,381 posts, almost all since 10 AM ET Thursday); BEA released the revision on its announced schedule and it was not a record (CNBC; Axios). The Jeffries deportation claim was the only carried card to rise in daytime hours (1,924 posts, 13.10×), widening into a 'far-left wish list' attack; he did tell PBS on Nov. 10 that wrongly deported DACA recipients should be brought back, which is narrower than the viral claim. Abrego Garcia cooled sharply (16,215, down from 38,923 this morning). On the Far Left, the Fetterman–Gillibrand backlash (1,742), the Van Hollen push (8,751) and Medicare for All (15,197) all eased on the holiday. One faded card (DSA-LA) was dropped and one was added. No card topic was on the U.S. trends list, which was all Thanksgiving and football. Every count, quote and fact-check comes from sources and X queries pulled this evening or carried over from this morning and labeled. Nothing here is invented.

oppositionNote.body: Right = narratives the Right is pushing after the Democratic midterm wave. Far Left = pressure on Democratic leadership and the incoming majority from the party's left. The new GDP card is tagged Right because it casts the midterm result as the product of 'fake' government data; it comes from the President himself. The Jeffries card recasts the incoming Speaker's agenda as returning deportees and a 'far-left wish list.' The USAID card casts a past Democratic administration's programs as a censorship operation. The Abrego Garcia card uses his departure to brand the Democrats who defended him. The Mamdani hotline card uses a city figure to brand the party. The Talarico, 'do not certify' and audit cards cast doubt on elections Democrats won. The Newsom card is the administration's attack on a Democratic governor. The Fetterman, Van Hollen and Medicare for All cards are pressure from the party's left on Democratic leaders. The tag is the primary opposition frame.

methodology: Last updated Thursday, Nov 26, 2026, 5:25 PM ET. This is a research snapshot for TDDR, not a live API, and it will go stale. U.S. X trends were pulled at about 5:14 PM ET. This morning's snapshot (Nov 26, 7:20 AM ET) is kept in the archive and was not overwritten. All twelve of its narratives were re-counted with the same queries so momentum compares like with like. The new 24-hour window overlaps this morning's by 14 hours (5 PM Wednesday to 7 AM Thursday ET), so each card also reports its 7 AM–5 PM ET Thursday daytime count against the same hours Wednesday. Thanksgiving lowered daytime volume on almost every query, so read 'cooling' with the holiday in mind. One card was dropped because it faded: DSA-LA (386 posts in the last 24 hours, 0.72× its prior daily average; this morning 1,108; 108 in Thursday's daytime hours versus 829 Wednesday). One card was added with a new query: Trump's 'fake economic numbers' GDP claim. Other candidates were counted and not carved out as cards: Trump's Thanksgiving call for Somalis on public assistance to be 'thrown out' of Minnesota (a Somali/Sharia query matched 3,944 posts in 24 hours, 0.40× a prior average swollen by last week's spike, with 3,430 in Thursday's daytime hours versus 1,503 Wednesday; Fox News and The Washington Times covered it; it is quoted on the GDP card); Eric Holder's remark on Nicolle Wallace's podcast that the 2028 nominee must pledge a 'DEI-infused nation' (Fox News, Nov. 26; a 'DEI-infused' or Holder-plus-DEI query matched 102 posts, 1.12×); and Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed's Schumer remark (1,022 posts, 0.52×; noted on the Medicare for All card).

For each narrative we ran one English-language X search with x.get_posts_counts_recent at hourly granularity over a 167-hour window from 6:00 PM ET Thursday, Nov 19, through 5:00 PM ET Thursday, Nov 26. The sum is the 'seven-day' total; the last 24 hours (5:00 PM ET Wednesday through 5:00 PM ET Thursday) are the 24-hour count; the last 10 hours give the Thursday daytime count, compared with hours 25–34 back (7 AM–5 PM ET Wednesday). Daily bars are those hourly counts summed by UTC day. We counted named news or fact-check outlets whose coverage we opened or retrieved and cite on the card. Official pages, transcripts, archives, aggregators, X News summaries and X posts are cited as sources but not counted as outlets; this evening that includes the Jeffries office PBS transcript, Trump's Truth archive and Trend Canopy. This evening we researched the new GDP card and re-researched the USAID and Jeffries cards; the Fetterman–DSCC and Medicare for All cards add X News summaries only; the other cards carry this morning's research and outlet counts and say so. No card topic was on the U.S. trends list.

Score = 50% volume index + 30% acceleration index + 20% coverage index. Volume index is 100 × log10(1 + last-24h posts) / log10(1 + the highest last-24h count in this set). Acceleration index is 100 × min(last-24h / prior daily average, 3) / 3, so a triple-or-higher average scores 100. Prior daily average is (seven-day total − last 24h) / 6. Coverage index is 70 × min(outlets, 7) / 7, plus 30 if the topic was on the U.S. X trends list when we pulled it. The USAID, GDP, Fetterman, Talarico and Jeffries queries had small baselines before this week, so their acceleration indexes are maxed out; the GDP multiple in the hundreds means 'new,' not 'hundreds of times bigger.' The volume ceiling this evening is 25,038 (the USAID query), down from 38,923 (Abrego Garcia) this morning, which raises every other card's volume index. Read the post counts alongside the scores.

Counts are query matches, not unique posts or unique users, and queries can overlap. The GDP query requires GDP, 'economic numbers,' 'fake numbers' or BEA plus a fraud or probe term plus Trump or election, so it catches news relays, market feeds and rebuttals of the claim. The other queries are unchanged from this morning and carry the same caveats: the USAID query catches rebuttals; the Abrego Garcia query catches news relays and his defenders; the Jeffries query catches unrelated ICE posts and left criticism of Jeffries; the Mamdani query catches explainers and translations; the Talarico query catches 'flipped Texas blue' celebrations; the Fetterman query catches primary news; the 'do not certify' query catches rebuttals and other countries' elections; the Medicare for All query catches supporters, opponents and unrelated 'M4A' uses; the Van Hollen query catches syndicated news. Replies are included. Sentiment is a qualitative label from relevancy-sorted post samples and from quotes in news coverage, not a scientific poll. This evening we pulled fresh samples for the GDP, USAID and Jeffries queries; the other cards carry this morning's sentiment and say so. disinfo.caveatBody: New this evening: 'Fake economic numbers just prior to the Election' / a 'RECORD SETTING ERROR' is false as stated. BEA released the Q3 revision from 3.4% to 4.3% on its previously announced schedule, not 'three weeks late'; the 0.9-point change was the largest since 2020 but tied for 16th since 1990 and smaller than a 1.2-point revision in Trump's first term (CNBC). Axios reported the claim of a 'purposeful' error was made without evidence; BEA attributed the change to updated software-price and retail-sales data. 'Jeffries will bring back the illegals Trump deported' still overstates what he said, but it has a real anchor: on PBS NewsHour on Nov. 10 he said 'Certainly' when asked about returning deported DACA recipients and called for 'remedial assistance' for people treated 'unfairly and unjustly' (his office's transcript; Fox News). That is not a plan to return all deportees, and no bill would do it. 'USAID got platforms to defund and deplatform outlets': a review of the release found no USAID award to GDI and no sign its pilot ran (The Media Now). Carried over from this morning: 'Jeffries promised to bring back the illegal aliens Trump deported' overstates an ambiguous moment. In the C-SPAN transcript of the Oct. 16 Pinecrest stop, Jeffries answered a question about returning people deported to third countries by calling for 'dramatic change' in enforcement and saying Trump's 'violent mass deportation machine does not get a dime'; the viral posts rest on a nod. We found no bill, budget or published Democratic plan to return deportees (Independence Journal; CBS Miami); the 'reparations' add-on in replies has no source. 'Gillibrand is stepping down from the DSCC' is not so: she has said she will seek another term, and the next Senate Democratic leader will name the chair after the Dec. 1 vote (The Hill; The Intercept argued she should be replaced). Carried over from earlier snapshots: 'Texas is being stolen' / 'apply the 0.85 algorithm and Paxton wins' has no evidence behind it. Texas's first statewide risk-limiting audit confirmed the Senate result with measured risk below 1% (Texas Scorecard); a federal judge dismissed the Potter County GOP's hand-count suit as 'speculation layered on speculation' (court order; San Antonio Current); and Paxton conceded on election night, so the circulating 'cannot accept' statement attributed to him is fabricated (Lead Stories). 'The DSCC endorsed Fetterman' is misleading: Gillibrand said the committee would back him in the general election if he wins the primary, and she did not endorse him in a primary (NBC News; Newsweek; The Philadelphia Inquirer). 'The USAID Files prove USAID got platforms to defund and deplatform outlets' goes beyond the documents: the most-cited item, a 2022 Global Disinformation Index concept note, is a proposal with no budget or award, and no public record shows USAID funded it (DC News Line); Newsweek said it is unclear which proposals were carried out. 'Mamdani is helping illegals evade ICE' describes a city legal-aid hotline that offers free immigration legal help; we found no rated fact-check, and the post itself does not urge anyone to evade enforcement (Townhall and LifeSiteNews quote it in full). Carried over from earlier snapshots: 'Abrego Garcia is an MS-13 gang member' is not supported; fact-checkers found the claim rested on a 2019 informant's account and his clothing, and that he had no criminal conviction (PolitiFact; USA Today; Snopes, 2025). '38 million invalid voters' is not a finding of illegal votes: the figure's own source, Unite4Freedom, describes the 38 million as 'registrations flagged for further investigation – not 38 million proven illegal registrations,' and we found no official finding that any state's result is in doubt (Democracy Docket; WOWT). 'Newsom is letting killers go free' is false: the commutations would change 548 death sentences to life without the possibility of parole, and none has taken effect pending the California Supreme Court (The National News Desk).

narratives.query: (GDP OR "economic numbers" OR "fake numbers" OR BEA) ("record setting" OR "RECORD SETTING" OR fake OR rigged OR purposeful OR investigate OR investigated OR investigation OR probe) (Trump OR election) lang:en
narratives.sentiment: Celebratory on the Right ('MOST SAVAGE THANKSGIVING MESSAGE OF ALL TIME'), with some posts asking whether the agency 'cooked' numbers to sink Republicans; market accounts and critics relay the CNBC correction
narratives.sentimentNote: In a relevancy sample of posts since 7 AM ET Thursday, the most-viewed was @GuntherEagleman's '🚨 TRUMP JUST DROPPED THE MOST SAVAGE THANKSGIVING MESSAGE OF ALL TIME!!… he thanked the people who put out FAKE economic numbers right before the election' (about 117,000 views, 5,564 likes, 1,753 reposts at sampling); copies of the same text came from @shadygrooove, @Texpatriot26 and others. @ConstitustionX asked 'DID GOVERNMENT AGENCY COOKED ECONOMIC NUMBERS TO REMOVE REPUBLICANS IN MID-TERMS?' (about 1,800 views) and @Mark_Twitchett wrote 'He says numbers are being RIGGED… Real growth or election manipulation?' Market and news accounts (@FirstSquawk, about 14,000 views; @CNBC, about 29,000) relayed the post; @SkylineReport's 'REALITY CHECK: THE GDP REVISION WAS SCHEDULED BEFORE THE ELECTION' (about 780 views) and @LordBullAI's 'BEA released it on its pre-announced schedule' carried the correction. One reply noted Trump 'hired the people that made the record setting error.' The sample was pulled at about 5:17 PM ET Thursday.
narratives.summary: New this evening. The query matched 7,381 posts in the last 24 hours (5 PM ET Wednesday to 5 PM ET Thursday), 250 times a near-zero prior daily average of about 30; 7,372 came from 7 AM to 5 PM ET Thursday, versus 30 in the same hours Wednesday. The busiest hour was 11 AM Thursday (1,550 posts). In a 10:45 AM ET Thanksgiving post on Truth Social, Trump wished a happy holiday 'to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late, showing that the GDP was actually 4.3%, versus 3.4%, A RECORD SETTING ERROR, and one so grave that it should be immediately investigated' (Trump's Truth archive). In a second post quoted by Axios he called it a 'massive, and purposeful, error' and asked, 'Why wasn't the correct number issued before the Election?' The Bureau of Economic Analysis revised third-quarter growth on Nov. 25 from its 3.4% advance estimate to 4.3%. CNBC reported the update came on the bureau's previously announced schedule, was the largest since 2020 but tied for 16th since 1990, and that the 3.4% advance figure released days before Election Day had already beaten forecasts. The same post also wished Thanksgiving to the 'Radical Far Left,' those 'looking to change our Court System to that of Sharia,' and said Somalis on government assistance in Minnesota 'should be thrown out' (The Washington Times; Rolling Stone).
talkingPoints: They put out fake economic numbers right before the election to sink Republicans — then quietly fixed them after.
A 'record setting error,' three weeks late: the midterm result was built on rigged data.
The deep state at the statistics agencies picked the winner; investigate now.
The real economy is booming — Democrats won on a lie about it.
narratives.amplifiers: Trump's own Truth Social posts; @GuntherEagleman and copy-paste accounts (@shadygrooove, @Texpatriot26, @wtcrescuer911); @ThePatriotOasis, @ConstitustionX, @JB_Slear. Relayed neutrally by market feeds (@FirstSquawk, @DeItaone per @ClosingPrints) and CNBC.
narratives.whyItWorks: It hands a beaten party a no-fault explanation for the midterm wave: the voters weren't wrong, the numbers were. The revision is real and unusually large, so the claim starts from a true fact, and few people know GDP is estimated three times on a fixed calendar. It came from the President on a holiday, wrapped in a viral, joke-like 'thank you' format that spread as entertainment. And it fits a familiar pattern after Trump's firing of the BLS commissioner last year, so the base already distrusts federal statistics.
narratives.audience: The Republican base looking for an explanation of the midterm losses; election-integrity audiences already sharing 'do not certify' and audit claims; and market-watchers, who saw the post relayed by financial feeds.
narratives.counter: Stick to the calendar. BEA publishes three estimates of each quarter about a month apart; the Nov. 25 second estimate came out on the date announced in advance (CNBC; Axios). The revision was large but not a record — tied for 16th since 1990, and smaller than the 1.2-point revision in 2020 during Trump's first term. The 'fake' pre-election number was already a strong 3.4% that beat forecasts, so it could not have been a plot to make the economy look bad. And BEA sits in a Commerce Department run by Trump's own secretary, Howard Lutnick (Axios).

factChecks.claim: The Q3 GDP revision from 3.4% to 4.3% was a 'RECORD SETTING ERROR' issued 'three weeks late.'
factChecks.detail: CNBC said Trump 'falsely deemed' the revision a mistake: it was released on BEA's previously announced schedule, was tied for 16th-largest since 1990, and was smaller than the 1.2-point revision in Q2 2020.

factChecks.claim: Pre-election GDP numbers were deliberately understated — a 'massive, and purposeful, error.'
factChecks.detail: Axios reported Trump made the allegation 'without evidence'; revisions are routine as fuller data arrive, and BEA explained this one by updated software-price and retail-sales data.

narratives.whyItWorks: It borrows the language of accountability. 'Audit' sounds like routine diligence, not an accusation, so people who would not say 'the election was stolen' can still sign on. It answers a real shock (Democrats winning statewide in Texas, Kansas and South Carolina) with an action people can take today: call, tag, sign. And because most people don't know their state already audits results, a demand for an audit sounds like something that hasn't happened.
narratives.audience: Trump voters in red states Democrats flipped, especially Texas; 2020 'stop the steal' veterans; election-integrity activists who backed the SAVE America Act; and voters angry at Senate Republicans who want someone to act before January.
narratives.counter: Agree with the premise and then point to the receipts: every state already audits its results, and Texas, under a 2021 Republican-passed law, is running its first statewide risk-limiting audit of the very Senate race people are questioning. Ask what a 'forensic audit' would check that the canvass, the hand-count audit and the risk-limiting audit don't. Note that Trump called the result a 'protest vote' against Senate Republicans. talkingPoints: Newsom stood with the murderers and the child slayers, not the families.
He waited until two days after the election to overrule 548 jury verdicts.
California voters kept the death penalty twice, and Newsom ignored them.
Trump is making sure the worst killers still face justice.
Democrats care more about monsters than victims.

Vince Fong (R-Calif.), @EricLDaugh (28,060 views on one post), @PeggyDodson, @NathanielSami, and accounts reviving Trump's 'Newscum' nickname. Fresno and Kern County district attorneys gave the critique a law-enforcement voice.
narratives.whyItWorks: It pairs a real, sweeping decision (all 548 death sentences) with named victims, many of them children, and puts grieving families in the room. Crime and punishment is one of the few issues where the Right still out-polls Democrats, and a lame-duck governor many see as a 2028 candidate is an easy national target. The 'he hid it until after the election' line turns a policy disagreement into a story about honesty. It also lets the Right change the subject from the midterm losses to Democrats and crime.
narratives.audience: Crime-focused conservatives and victims' advocates; California Republicans and some prosecutors; swing voters who support the death penalty for the worst crimes; and 2028 opponents of Newsom on both sides.
narratives.counter: Don't defend the killers. Defend the facts and the families' right to finality. No one is being released: the sentences become life without parole, and the California Supreme Court must approve commutations for anyone with more than one felony, so none have taken effect. Trump's order covers federal cases, not California's death row. And point out the contrast Newsom drew himself: a president who pardons allies is lecturing others about mercy.
